exercises.title: A small beginning
exercises.instructions: Add fifty source word units to the manuscript in Drafting mode. Typing and deliberate paste count; historical restoration is recorded separately. The measured criterion is quantity, not literary quality.

exercises.title: Keyboard-only warm-up
exercises.instructions: Build one hundred word units with the keyboard in Drafting mode. Pasted words and undo/redo do not satisfy this keyboard-addition target. Rewriting is welcome; no deletion penalty is imposed.

exercises.title: A longer opening
exercises.instructions: Add three hundred source word units in Drafting mode. Use a scene you genuinely want to explore. You may stop or reroll without a streak penalty; this is a measured input target, not an assessment of the scene.

exercises.title: The wrong delivery
exercises.instructions: Write a short scene in which a harmless parcel reaches the only person who cannot safely open it. Let the misunderstanding change what the recipient does next. Mark completion yourself after trying it.

exercises.title: The promise with a price
exercises.instructions: Draft a moment when keeping a kind promise would hurt someone uninvolved. Give the viewpoint character a concrete choice rather than explaining the moral in narration. Completion is self-reported.

exercises.title: A useful failure
exercises.instructions: Let a character fail at a practical task and discover a reason to welcome that failure. Connect the changed attitude to a later action, not a speech about lessons learned. Judge the attempt yourself.

exercises.title: The borrowed habit
exercises.instructions: Show a character unconsciously using a habit learned from someone they now avoid. Choose a physical action small enough to fit into an ordinary encounter. Self-report when you have explored it.

exercises.title: A boundary under pressure
exercises.instructions: Give a character a boundary they can state easily but struggle to maintain with a particular person. Put both people in a situation that makes the boundary inconvenient. Self-report the experiment.

exercises.title: A rival acts generously
exercises.instructions: Have a rival perform a genuinely generous act that complicates the protagonist's account of them. Preserve a real disagreement; generosity need not erase conflict. Completion is your judgment.

exercises.title: An expired opportunity
exercises.instructions: Turn a routine discovery into an opportunity with a visible expiration time. Decide what the character must give up to act before that deadline. Self-report after outlining or drafting the turn.

exercises.title: The consequence arrives early
exercises.instructions: Move a consequence the protagonist expected much later into the next scene. Change the available choices rather than merely increasing the amount of danger. Completion is self-reported.

exercises.title: Two reasonable plans collide
exercises.instructions: Build a reversal caused by two people following reasonable but incompatible plans. Trace the causal chain without relying on a random accident. Self-report once the chain can be explained.

exercises.title: An answer made of objects
exercises.instructions: Write an exchange in which one speaker answers a difficult question by handling nearby objects. Let the other speaker notice or misread the gesture. Self-report the attempt; no automatic style score is used.

exercises.title: The safe subject
exercises.instructions: Give two speakers an important shared problem they discuss through an apparently safe topic. Make their different goals legible without spelling out every implication. Completion is self-reported.

exercises.title: A third listener
exercises.instructions: Rework a conversation when an unexpected third person begins listening. Let each original speaker adapt differently, changing what can safely be said. Judge completion yourself.

exercises.title: Evidence of the absent
exercises.instructions: Describe a room through evidence of a person who has just left it. Avoid summarizing that person's entire biography; select details relevant to the observer. Self-report when the exercise is attempted.

exercises.title: A place changes function
exercises.instructions: Describe the same public place before and after it is repurposed for an emergency. Keep its geography consistent while changing what details matter. Completion is self-reported.

exercises.title: An unreliable sense
exercises.instructions: Build a setting description around one sense that cannot currently be trusted. Give the character a practical way to test an assumption about the place. Self-report the exploration.

exercises.title: A different witness
exercises.instructions: Retell a brief event from a witness who misses its most important action. Let their limited information create a different but internally coherent account. Self-report the experiment.

exercises.title: Distance without explanation
exercises.instructions: Draft one paragraph close to a character's immediate perception and another at a greater narrative distance. Keep the event unchanged; compare the effects yourself. Completion is self-reported.

exercises.title: Knowledge withheld fairly
exercises.instructions: Write a scene where the viewpoint character knows a fact the reader does not yet know. Avoid false statements inside their thoughts; decide how to reveal the fact fairly. Self-report your attempt.

exercises.title: Five deliberate editor changes
exercises.instructions: Switch to Revision mode and make five actual text-changing editor operations in a manuscript source. Quantity is measured; usefulness is not. Your normal undo and original-source save safeguards remain available.

exercises.title: Repair a causal hinge
exercises.instructions: Find a passage where an action appears without a sufficient reason. Revise its setup or its consequence so the causal hinge is readable. Use a checkpoint if desired; completion is self-reported.

exercises.title: Remove an explanation safely
exercises.instructions: Keep a checkpoint, then remove an explanation and strengthen the observable evidence that replaces it. Compare both versions before deciding which to keep. Self-report completion; no automatic quality ranking is claimed.

exercises.title: Read for a missing question
exercises.instructions: Read a short passage without editing. Note one question a reader might reasonably have at its end, in an ordinary note of your choice. Completion is self-reported, not inferred from leaving the app open.

exercises.title: Follow a physical object
exercises.instructions: Read several scenes and trace one object's location and custody. Record any uncertainty without silently correcting the manuscript. Self-report after following the trail.

exercises.title: Listen for a change in intention
exercises.instructions: Read a chapter and identify where the viewpoint character's intention changes. Distinguish an explicit change from your interpretation. Completion is self-reported; elapsed timer time is not proof of reading.

exercises.title: A map and an apology
exercises.instructions: Premise: a corrected map would invalidate a public apology. Exercise: draft a conversation in which someone asks for the correction while wanting to preserve the apology. Self-report the attempt. This is one original combined prompt, not a 1,000-item plot corpus.

exercises.title: The borrowed authority
exercises.instructions: Premise: an ordinary person temporarily inherits the power to settle a neighborhood dispute. Exercise: show their first decision through someone who distrusts that authority. Completion is self-reported.

exercises.title: A rescue with incompatible endings
exercises.instructions: Premise: two groups agree that a missing person must be rescued but disagree about where safety lies. Exercise: plot a scene in which the rescued person changes both groups' plans. Self-report the experiment.
